rationale: bugs_open/238 §11.11, owner-ruled 2026-08-21. `contact-block` declares its email field as `site_specs.contact.email`; the platform stores that fact as `site_specs.identity.email` / the `sites.email` column; and the resolver's bridge between the two is HARD-GATED to one aspect name — `resolveSpecAlias` step 2 is literally `if aspect != "identity" { return nil, false }`, with `siteRowIdentityColumns` mapping leaf `email` onto the `sites.email` column. So `identity.email` resolves and `contact.email`, the same fact under a different spelling, has returned not-found on every site on every build since the component was written. Measured, and the blast radius IS the damage: exactly ONE active component declares `contact.email` (this one) and exactly ONE declares `identity.email` (which works); `contact_email` on `contact-block` is 6 deployed rows across 3 sites and ALL 6 are missing the key; and those 6 are precisely 6 of the 9 unqueued (page, slot) pairs the STRUCTURAL_KEY_CARRY_MISS findings name. `function='contact-block'` has exactly one active row, so there is no fork to skip (RFC_034: convert by id, never by function). WHY REPOINT THE FIELD RATHER THAN WIDEN THE RESOLVER: widening the alias so any aspect may read the sites row is a shared-seam change to a function every build flows through — bigger blast radius, RFC-shaped, and it would take the publish-this-address question fleet-wide in one step. Repointing one field is one row, no Go, no roll, reversible, and it aligns this component with the sibling spelling that already works. Reuse the working spelling; do not widen the mechanism to accommodate the broken one. THE OWNER DECISION THIS RESTS ON, recorded because the code cannot justify it: every address this publishes is `<site>@contactforsales.com`, a pattern on 15 of 44 live sites — systematic enough to look platform-assigned rather than a client's inbox. Publishing a reachable address merely because it is reachable is bugs_open/140's defect exactly (a contact component served an invented info@example.com on eight live sites). It was put to the owner and the ruling on 2026-08-21 was: "yes, that email should appear on contact pages". Without that ruling this must not be applied. PARTIAL BY DESIGN, so a partial result is not read as a partial failure: leopardess resolves at the literal path (4 pairs), robot-hands via the sites-row alias (1 pair), and gamesdesign resolves NOTHING because that site has no email in either place — 1 pair stays unresolved and becomes an honest data gap for a human rather than a resolver bug.

plan.summary: Point content_components 4ebdccb5 (`contact-block`) `input_schema.fields.contact_email.source` from the unreachable `site_specs.contact.email` to `site_specs.identity.email`, which the resolver can reach both literally and via its sites-row alias. One row, no Go, reversible. Config is live on apply but the six pages are NOT changed until each is re-rendered, so applying this alone is inert at the artefact.
grounded_in: the gate itself: plan_sections_action.go resolveSpecAlias step 2 — `// 2. The canonical sites row.` then `if aspect != "identity" { return nil, false }`; and `siteRowIdentityColumns` maps "email" -> "email"
two spellings, one fact: exactly 1 active component declares site_specs.contact.email (contact-block, id 4ebdccb5-6eb0-4b03-9fe1-0fa5cc315fb4) and exactly 1 declares site_specs.identity.email
the damage equals the blast radius: contact_email on contact-block = 6 deployed rows, 3 sites, 6 of 6 missing the key
no fork to skip: SELECT count(*) FROM content_components WHERE function='contact-block' AND COALESCE(is_active,true) -> 1

resolution is DETERMINISTIC despite 29/11/3 historical identity rows: ensureSpecs loads WHERE is_current=true and takes the LAST row per aspect with no ORDER BY, and each of the three sites has exactly ONE current identity row

per-site outcome measured before writing: leopardess current identity row HAS email (literal path); robot-hands has no identity.email leaf but sites.email is populated (alias step 2); gamesdesign has neither (will still not resolve — correct)
the placeholder question is real, not hypothetical: 15 of 44 live sites carry an @contactforsales.com address (26 empty, 3 other domains) — systematic, hence put to the owner rather than assumed

no carry interaction: the six stored rows do not hold contact_email at all, so there is no stored value for PBP-039 to prefer; and live resolution wins regardless, the carry running only after the literal path and every alias have missed

edits.rationale: Repoint one field at the reachable spelling. Pre-flight asserts the single active row, the field, and the CURRENT source before any write, because a jsonb_set on a moved shape creates a branch and reports success. create_missing is FALSE deliberately: the key must already exist and the pre-flight proved it does, so a missing key is a moved schema rather than something to add. Verify asserts the source moved AND that type/required survived — jsonb_set replaces a subtree, and a path typo would silently drop the neighbours while the source read fine — plus a NOTICE census of any other active component still declaring a site_specs.contact.* source, since that aspect has never existed on any site.
edits.sketch: BEGIN; \echo BEFORE; DO $$ assert 1 active contact-block row (else RAISE naming RFC_034 fork rule) and contact_email.source = 'site_specs.contact.email' (else RAISE: already applied or schema moved) $$; UPDATE content_components SET input_schema = jsonb_set(input_schema,'{fields,contact_email,source}','"site_specs.identity.email"',false) WHERE id='4ebdccb5-...'; \echo AFTER; DO $$ verify source moved, type='text' and required IS TRUE intact, NOTICE on remaining site_specs.contact.* declarers $$; COMMIT; then a WATCH section: the per-site will-resolve-to query, the page_rerender (reason=section_data_resolved) needed to reach the artefact, and the divergence check first per bugs_open/229.

plan.risks: The address published is <site>@contactforsales.com on 15 of 44 sites and may be a platform-assigned lead-capture address rather than a client's inbox — publishing it because it is reachable is bugs_open/140's defect. Mitigated only by the owner's explicit 2026-08-21 ruling, which is quoted in the file header; without it the file must not be applied. Config is live on apply but no page changes until re-rendered, so 'applied' will not equal 'visible' — the header says so and the WATCH section carries the re-render step and the bugs_open/229 divergence check that must precede it. gamesdesign.co.uk will still not resolve (no email in either store). That is the correct outcome and is stated per-site in the header so a 5-of-6 result is not read as a partial failure. Reverting is NOT symmetrical and the ROLLBACK header says so: site_specs.contact.email resolves nowhere, so reverting restores a broken state deliberately; and it does not unpublish an address already re-rendered into content_data and deployed HTML — that needs the key cleared AND a re-render, and clearing only one of the two lets the PBP-039 carry re-supply it.
plan.non_scope: Not widening resolveSpecAlias to let any aspect read the sites row — shared-seam, RFC-shaped, and it would take the placeholder question fleet-wide. Not re-rendering the six pages in this change: config and artefact are sequenced separately on purpose, and each page needs its divergence stamp checked first (bugs_open/229). Not touching the other 3 of the 9 residual pairs: gamesdesign's cta.primary_url, leopardess's contact.cta_url, and fundamentallyai's six fields the component's schema no longer declares (bugs_open/309's class). Not minting review-queue items for any of them — six items that this one decision closes is the churn the two-strike rule punishes.
